explanations.explanation: That's the one, baker. God says it's “…an altar of acacia wood for the burning of incense.” That's its whole job. Some tools are made for one thing and do it well, like my stamper handle, which has never once tried to be a spatula.

Close, because grain offerings do belong at an altar. But God says this altar is for burning incense. He also says no grain offering is to be offered on it (Exodus 30:9). So this one has a single job, friend, and it's not that one.

I see why you'd pick it. Offerings were a big part of all these plans. But for this altar God says it's for burning incense. He even says, "nor are you to pour a drink offering on it" (Exodus 30:9). Pouring is not what it's built for.

explanations.answer: God will meet with Moses there
explanations.explanation: Right on the money, baker. God says the altar goes before the veil and the mercy seat, “…where I will meet with you.” He's speaking to Moses, Israel's leader. It's a special spot, so it's worth getting the placement exactly right.

That's a fair guess, since leaders gathering is a common thing. But it isn't what God says about this spot. He says the altar goes “…where I will meet with you.” He's speaking to Moses there, and the elders don't come into it.

explanations.answer: The people will bring gifts there
explanations.explanation: Gifts are a big theme in these plans, so I get it. But God doesn't say that about this place. He says it's “…where I will meet with you.” Moses, Israel's leader, is the one He's talking to. It's about God meeting with him.

True! God says Aaron “…must burn the incense perpetually before the LORD for the generations to come.” Aaron is Moses' brother, and this is his job. "Generations to come" means this isn't a one-week project. This is a long, long commitment.

It's actually true. God says Aaron, Moses' brother, “…must burn the incense perpetually before the LORD for the generations to come.” So the burning isn't a one-time thing. It keeps going for generations.

This one's false, friend. God says, “On this altar you must not offer unauthorized incense or a burnt offering or grain offering…” That's a plain no on burnt offerings. This altar has a single job, and incense is it.

False is right, baker. God says, “On this altar you must not offer unauthorized incense or a burnt offering or grain offering…” Burnt offerings are a no here. I've put the wrong dough in the wrong pan before, but God's instructions here are very clear.
Plague is the word. God says, “Then no plague will come upon them when they are numbered.” Each man pays a ransom for his life when he's counted. It's a short verse with a lot of weight in it.
A famine is a scary thing, so I see the pull. But that isn't the word God uses here. He says the ransom is paid so that “…no plague will come upon them when they are numbered.” The word is plague.

War is a heavy word, and I can see why it came to mind. But God doesn't say that here. He says that when each man pays his ransom, “…no plague will come upon them when they are numbered.” So plague is the word in the blank.

explanations.answer: The service of the Tent of Meeting
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. God says to take the atonement money and “…use it for the service of the Tent of Meeting.” He also says it serves as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD. And remember, the rich don't give more than a half shekel and the poor don't give less (Exodus 30:15).

That's not what God says. He tells Moses to take the atonement money “…and use it for the service of the Tent of Meeting.” An army isn't mentioned anywhere in these verses. The money goes to the Tent of Meeting.

explanations.answer: Gifts for the poor in Israel
explanations.explanation: That's a kind guess, friend. But God doesn't say that in these verses. He says to use the atonement money “…for the service of the Tent of Meeting.” The poor do give the same half shekel as everyone else (Exodus 30:15).

explanations.answer: For Aaron and his sons to wash
explanations.explanation: That's right! The water is the washing station for Aaron and his sons, who are to wash their hands and feet there. God sets the basin between the Tent of Meeting and the altar. Think of it like the sink right by the oven, so nobody has to go looking.
Water is good for drinking, so I get it. But that isn't what God says this basin is for. He says Aaron and his sons “…are to wash their hands and feet.” The basin is for their washing.

Interesting guess, baker. I know all about mixing things in. But God never says the water is mixed into the offerings. He says it's for Aaron and his sons “…to wash their hands and feet.” It's a washing basin.

explanations.answer: So that they will not die
explanations.explanation: You got it, baker. God says, “…they must wash with water so that they will not die.” He says it twice, in verses 20 and 21. When God says something twice, I write it down once and underline it twice. He also calls it “…a permanent statute for Aaron and his descendants for the generations to come.”

explanations.answer: So that the people will trust them
explanations.explanation: That sounds reasonable, but it isn't the reason God gives. He says they are to wash their hands and feet “…so that they will not die.” The text doesn't mention the people's trust. God gives this reason, and He gives it twice.

explanations.answer: So that the altar will stay clean
explanations.explanation: A clean altar sounds like a good reason, I'll admit. But the reason God gives is about the priests themselves: “…so that they will not die.” He repeats it in verse 21. I'd stick with the reason He actually states.

Yes, baker! God says, “Prepare from these a sacred anointing oil, a fragrant blend, the work of a perfumer…” The spices go together with olive oil in this blend. It's a special recipe, and the instructions are specific.

Oil and lamps do go together in this story, so I see why you'd choose that. But for these spices, God says, “Prepare from these a sacred anointing oil…” The blend is for anointing. The text doesn't say it's for the lampstand's light.

That's a thoughtful guess, but it's not what God says. He tells Moses, “Prepare from these a sacred anointing oil, a fragrant blend, the work of a perfumer…” The text names this blend an anointing oil. Healing wounds isn't mentioned.
True! God says to consecrate these things “…so that they will be most holy. Whatever touches them shall be holy.” That's a strong statement. They're set apart in a serious way.
It's true, friend. After the anointing, God says, “Whatever touches them shall be holy.” He calls these things most holy. So that line stays right where it is.
That's it, baker. God tells Moses to anoint Aaron and his sons and “…consecrate them to serve Me as priests.” The same oil that anoints the furnishings anoints them too. Priests is the word.
Judges is a real job in the Bible, so I see why you'd pick it. But here God says to anoint Aaron and his sons “…and consecrate them to serve Me as priests.” The word in the blank is priests.
Prophets matter a lot in Scripture, so I get the guess. But that isn't the word here. God says to anoint Aaron and his sons “…and consecrate them to serve Me as priests.” Priests fills the blank.

This one's false, friend. God says, “It must not be used to anoint an ordinary man, and you must not make anything like it with the same formula.” He adds, “It is holy, and it must be holy to you.” No copycat batches allowed.
False is right, baker. God says, “…you must not make anything like it with the same formula.” He also says, “It is holy, and it must be holy to you.” I'd never copy a formula God says to leave alone.

explanations.answer: He will be cut off from his people
explanations.explanation: That's right, baker. God says anyone who mixes perfume like it or puts it on an outsider “…shall be cut off from his people.” That's a serious warning. God is showing how holy this oil is.

explanations.answer: He will pay a fine of a half shekel
explanations.explanation: That half shekel is a good thing to remember, but it belongs to the census (Exodus 30:13). For mixing perfume like the sacred oil, God says, “…shall be cut off from his people.” No fine is mentioned here.

explanations.answer: He will bring a bull as an offering
explanations.explanation: Offerings show up a lot in these plans, so it's an understandable pick. But in this verse God doesn't mention a bull. He says anyone who mixes perfume like the oil or puts it on an outsider “…shall be cut off from his people.”

This one is false, friend. God says, “You are never to use this formula to make incense for yourselves…” Then He adds, “Anyone who makes something like it to enjoy its fragrance shall be cut off from his people.” Making it for fragrance alone is a clear no.

False is right, baker. God says, “You are never to use this formula to make incense for yourselves; you shall regard it as holy to the LORD.” Anyone who makes it to enjoy its fragrance “…shall be cut off from his people.” That's a serious line.
